title_en: Passport Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of regulating the application, issuance and administration of passports of the People's Republic of China, safeguarding the rights and interests of citizens of the People's Republic of China to enter and exit the national territory of the People's Republic of China, and promoting international exchanges.

Article 2 The passport of the People's Republic of China shall be the document for citizens of the People's Republic of China to enter and exit the national territory and to certify their nationality and identity abroad.
No organization or individual may forge, alter, transfer, intentionally damage, or illegally detain a passport.

Article 3 Passports are divided into ordinary passports, diplomatic passports and service passports.
Passports shall be recommended by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to foreign governments through diplomatic channels.

Article 4 Ordinary passports shall be issued by the exit and entry administration department of the Ministry of Public Security, or by the exit and entry administration departments of the public security organs of the local people's governments at or above the county level authorized by the Ministry of Public Security, as well as by the embassies and consulates of the People's Republic of China abroad and other overseas agencies authorized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Diplomatic passports shall be issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Service passports shall be issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the embassies and consulates of the People's Republic of China abroad or other overseas agencies authorized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and by the foreign affairs departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government and cities divided into districts authorized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Article 5 Where a citizen goes abroad for non-official reasons such as settling down abroad, visiting relatives, studying, employment, traveling, or engaging in business activities, he or she shall apply for an ordinary passport in person to the exit and entry administration department of the public security organ of the local people's government at or above the county level in the place of his or her registered residence.

Article 6 A citizen applying for an ordinary passport shall submit his or her resident identity card, household registration booklet, recent bareheaded photos and relevant materials concerning the reason for the application. Where a state functionary applies for an ordinary passport for exit for the reasons specified in Article 5 of this Law, he or she shall also submit relevant certifying documents in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
The exit and entry administration department of the public security organ shall issue an ordinary passport within fifteen days from the date of receiving the application materials; if it refuses to issue a passport because the application does not meet the provisions, it shall state the reasons in writing and notify the applicant of the right to apply for administrative reconsideration or bring an administrative action according to law.
Where a passport cannot be issued on time due to remote areas or areas with inconvenient transportation or due to special circumstances, the time for issuance may be extended to thirty days upon the approval of the person in charge of the passport issuing authority.
Where a citizen requests expedited processing due to reasonable urgent reasons, the exit and entry administration department of the public security organ shall handle it promptly.

Article 7 The registered items of an ordinary passport shall include: the name, sex, date of birth and place of birth of the passport holder, and the date of issuance, validity period, place of issuance and issuing authority of the passport.
The validity period of an ordinary passport shall be: five years for a passport holder under the age of sixteen, and ten years for a passport holder aged sixteen or above.
The specific measures for issuing ordinary passports shall be prescribed by the Ministry of Public Security.

Article 8 Diplomatic passports shall be used by diplomatic officers, consular officers, their accompanying spouses, minor children and diplomatic couriers.
Service passports shall be used by staff members sent by the Chinese Government to work in the embassies and consulates of the People's Republic of China abroad, or in the United Nations, its specialized agencies and other intergovernmental international organizations, as well as their accompanying spouses and minor children.
Where a citizen other than those specified in the preceding two paragraphs goes abroad for official duties, his or her work unit shall submit an application to the foreign affairs department in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 4 of this Law, and the foreign affairs department shall, as needed, issue a diplomatic passport or a service passport.

Article 9 The registered items of diplomatic passports and service passports shall include: the name, sex, date of birth and place of birth of the passport holder, and the date of issuance, validity period and issuing authority of the passport.
The scope of issuance, issuance measures, validity period of diplomatic passports and service passports, as well as the specific categories of service passports, shall be prescribed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Article 10 Where the registered items of the passport held by a passport holder change, he or she shall apply to the passport issuing authority for an endorsement of alteration on the passport by submitting relevant certifying materials.

Article 12 A passport shall have both visual reading and machine reading functions.
The anti-counterfeiting performance of passports shall be formulated with reference to international technical standards.
Passport issuing authorities and their staff members shall keep confidential the personal information of citizens that they have learned in the course of producing and issuing passports.

Article 15 A People's Court, a People's Procuratorate, a public security organ, a national security organ, or an administrative supervision organ may, as necessary for handling a case, detain the passport of a party to the case according to law.
If the party to the case refuses to hand over the passport, the state organ specified in the preceding paragraph may request the passport issuing authority to declare the passport of the party to the case null and void.

Article 16 Where a passport holder loses the nationality of the People's Republic of China, or the passport is lost or stolen, the passport issuing authority shall declare the passport null and void.
Passports that are forged, altered, obtained by fraud, or declared null and void by the issuing authority shall be invalid.

Article 17 Anyone who practices fraud to obtain a passport shall have his or her passport confiscated or declared null and void by the passport issuing authority; and shall be fined not less than RMB 2,000 yuan but not more than RMB 5,000 yuan by the public security organ; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 18 Anyone who provides another person with a forged or altered passport, or sells a passport, shall be subject to criminal liability according to law; if the act is not serious enough for criminal punishment, the public security organ shall confiscate the illegal gains, impose a detention of not less than ten days but not more than fifteen days, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than RMB 2,000 yuan but not more than RMB 5,000 yuan; the illegal passports and their printing equipment shall be confiscated by the public security organ.

Article 19 Anyone who uses a forged or altered passport or fraudulently uses another person's passport to enter or exit the national (border) territory shall be penalized by the public security organ in accordance with the provisions of the law on exit and entry administration; the illegal passports shall be confiscated by the public security organ.

Article 21 The Ministry of Public Security shall prescribe the pattern and supervise the production of ordinary passports; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall prescribe the pattern and supervise the production of diplomatic passports and service passports.

Article 22 Passport issuing authorities may collect fees for the cost of passports and for endorsements. The fees collected for the cost of passports and for endorsements shall be turned over to the State Treasury.
The standards for the cost of passports and endorsement fees shall be prescribed and published by the price administration department of the State Council jointly with the finance department of the State Council.

Article 23 Where a citizen going abroad for a short period loses his or her passport, or the passport is stolen or damaged and cannot be used abroad, he or she shall apply to the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China abroad or to another overseas agency authorized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a Travel Permit of the People's Republic of China.

Article 24 Where a citizen engages in border trade, border tourism services, or participates in border tourism, he or she may apply to the exit and entry administration department of the public security organ of the local people's government at or above the county level authorized by the Ministry of Public Security for an Exit-Entry Permit of the People's Republic of China.

Article 25 Where a citizen enters or exits the national territory as a seafarer and works on board a vessel abroad, he or she shall apply to the maritime administration agency authorized by the Ministry of Transport for a Seafarer's Passport of the People's Republic of China.
Article 26 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2007. Passports issued prior to the coming into force of this Law shall remain valid within their validity period.
